title: Launch or formalise a business
who_for: Anyone with a business idea, or a business that runs on handshakes and needs to be made official.
loving_god: We bring our plans to God each week and start with honesty about what we can and cannot do.
loving_others: We test each other's ideas, share what we learn about the law and the market, and cheer every first step.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a registered or clearly planned business, a business account and a first sale or a dated plan for one.
week12_outcome: A registered or clearly planned business, and a first sale or a dated plan for one.
arc: Write down who your first ten customers are and what problem you solve for each of them.
Take the next legal or practical step: register the name with the CAC, open a business account or make your first sale.
Set a 90-day plan with one revenue target, and ask one person in the tribe to check on it monthly.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or investment advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has started or formalised a business and remembers what the first steps cost. Keeps a group moving week to week.

title: Grow revenue and systems
who_for: Owners whose business works but depends on them, and who want steady growth without losing their family or their faith.
loving_god: We commit our work to God each week and ask for wisdom on one decision at a time.
loving_others: We share our numbers with each other honestly, borrow each other's best methods and carry each other's pressure.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us tracks one health number every week, has one process someone else can run and has talked with our best customers.
week12_outcome: One weekly number tracked, one process handed over, and a plan built on what the best customers value.
arc: Pick one number that tells you if the business is healthy and record it every week.
Write down one process that depends only on you and make it simple enough for someone else to do.
Ask your five best customers what they value most, then do more of it.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or investment advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has grown a business past the founder stage and put simple systems in place. Asks good questions about numbers.

title: Validate my idea with real customers
who_for: Anyone with a business idea who has not yet asked the people who would pay for it.
loving_god: We bring our ideas to God before we pour our savings into them, and we listen for correction as much as for approval.
loving_others: We role-play customer conversations, say what we heard honestly and never flatter an idea to protect a feeling.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has spoken with at least fifteen possible customers and made a clear go, change or stop decision with evidence.
week12_outcome: Fifteen customer conversations and a written go, change or stop decision.
arc: Write the problem your idea solves and who has it. List twenty people who fit and book five short conversations.
Hold ten more conversations. Ask what they do now, what it costs them and what they would pay. Do not pitch. Write down their exact words.
Sort what you heard into patterns. Decide to go, change or stop, and share the evidence and your decision with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not promise that an idea will succeed or fail. They help members gather evidence and decide for themselves.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has tested an idea before building it, and can hear 'no' without taking it personally.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have talked to real customers and I know whether this idea is worth my money.
By week 12, I have changed my idea because of what I heard, and I'm glad I asked.
By week 12, I have a clear decision and people who helped me make it.

title: Register my business and open a business account
who_for: Anyone running a business informally who is ready to make it official.
loving_god: We ask God for courage to do the dull, necessary steps and we honour the rules of the land.
loving_others: We share what each office, form and bank asked for, go through the steps together and tell each other the real costs.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has the registration steps done or booked, a separate business account and a simple habit of keeping business money apart from personal money.
week12_outcome: Registration done or booked, a separate business account, and business money kept apart.
arc: List what your business needs to be official: name, registration, tax number and account. Put a date and a cost next to each item.
Complete or book the next two items. Share what you learned so the next person in the tribe saves time.
Open the business account and move one week of business money into it. Write a one-page rule for keeping the two kinds of money apart.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or investment advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has registered a business in Nigeria and can explain the steps in plain words.

member_outcomes: By week 12, my business is registered, or I have a booked date, and I know what it cost.
By week 12, I have a business account and I no longer mix it with my own money.
By week 12, the paperwork no longer frightens me and I know my next step.

title: Win my first ten paying customers
who_for: Anyone with something to sell who has fewer than ten customers.
loving_god: We bring our business to God each week, and we price, promise and pay with honesty.
loving_others: We test each other's offers, introduce each other to customers, and celebrate every sale together.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has ten paying customers, a simple sales record and a weekly selling habit.
week12_outcome: Ten paying customers, or the target the member set in week 1.
arc: List twenty people who might need what you sell and talk to five of them this week. Ask what they would pay for.
Make one clear offer with a price and sell it to ten people. Write down every yes, every no and the reason given.
Keep a simple sales record, repeat what worked and drop what did not. Ask your best customer for one introduction.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal or tax advice. They point to a professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has sold to real customers and remembers how hard the first ten were.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have ten paying customers, or I'm close and I know why.
By week 12, I sell every week and no longer wait for customers to find me.
By week 12, I have a sales record and a clear offer I'm not ashamed of.

title: Price my offer and stop undercharging
who_for: Owners who suspect they charge too little and are afraid to say a higher number.
loving_god: We ask God to free us from fear of people and from the love of money, and to price with fairness.
loving_others: We practise saying our prices aloud, ask each other hard questions and refuse to let anyone apologise for fair pay.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us knows what each offer costs us to deliver, has a written price list and has quoted the new prices to at least three customers.
week12_outcome: A written price list built on real costs, and new prices quoted to three customers.
arc: Work out what one sale really costs you in time, materials and tax. Write your current price next to it and look at the gap.
Write a price list with a reason beside each price. Practise saying every price aloud to someone in the tribe until it sounds calm.
Quote the new prices to three customers and write down what each said. Keep the price unless you hear a reason to change it.
guardrail: Leaders do not set another member's price or give financial advice. They ask questions and let the member decide.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has raised prices and kept customers. Can talk about money without shame.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I know what my work costs and I charge more fairly for it.
By week 12, I can say my price without apologising.
By week 12, I have a price list and customers who accepted it.

title: Hire and manage my first employee
who_for: Owners who are about to hire, or who hired someone and are struggling to lead them.
loving_god: We ask God to help us treat every worker as a person He made, and to pay and speak with fairness.
loving_others: We share what worked and what failed when we hired, role-play hard conversations and keep each other honest about how we treat staff.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written role for the first hire, a clear way to pay and review them, and one weekly check-in kept.
week12_outcome: A written role, a fair pay and review plan, and a weekly check-in kept for a month.
arc: Write what the first hire must do in five lines, and what you will stop doing yourself. Ask one owner in the tribe to read it.
Draft the offer: pay, hours, duties and trial period. Role-play the interview and the first day with someone in the tribe.
Hold a short weekly check-in with your hire. Write what is working and what is not, and share one lesson with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give employment law, payroll or tax advice. They send members to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has hired and led staff in a small business and can speak plainly about getting it wrong.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have hired someone, or I'm ready to, and the role is clear.
By week 12, I lead my first employee with fairness and a weekly rhythm.
By week 12, I no longer do everything myself and I still sleep.

title: Keep clean books and pay my taxes on time
who_for: Owners whose records live in their head or in a pile of receipts.
loving_god: We believe honest accounts honour God and we ask Him to keep us from hiding anything.
loving_others: We swap simple templates, remind each other of deadlines and encourage each other to ask a professional for help.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us records every sale and cost weekly, knows what tax is due and when, and has booked help where we need it.
week12_outcome: Weekly records kept for the season, tax dates written down, and any professional help booked.
arc: Gather every receipt and bank record from the last month into one place. Choose a simple way to record sales and costs.
Record every sale and cost each week for a month. Find out which taxes and filings apply to you and write down the dates.
Book time with an accountant for anything you cannot settle yourself. Set a calendar reminder for every date you wrote.
guardrail: Leaders do not give tax, audit or accounting advice. They share simple habits and point to a qualified accountant.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Keeps tidy books for a business and is patient with people who find numbers frightening.

member_outcomes: By week 12, my records are up to date and I know what I owe and when.
By week 12, I have stopped dreading my books.
By week 12, I have paid what was due on time, or booked help to do so.

title: Raise capital or a grant
who_for: Owners with a clear plan who need outside money and do not know where to start.
loving_god: We ask God to guard our hearts from greed and from desperation, and to show us what is enough.
loving_others: We read each other's plans, ask the questions a funder would ask and share honest leads without hoarding them.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written plan with real numbers, a list of suitable funders and at least two applications or conversations done.
week12_outcome: A plan with real numbers, a list of suitable funders, and two applications or conversations done.
arc: Write what you need the money for, how much and what it will change. Put the numbers in one page.
List ten possible funders, grants or investors and read what each one asks for. Choose three that truly fit you.
Complete two applications or conversations. Share what you were asked and what you would answer differently.
guardrail: Leaders do not give investment or legal advice or promise that money will come. They help members prepare honestly.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has applied for a grant or raised money, including being turned down, and stayed honest in the process.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I know exactly how much I need and what for.
By week 12, I have applied or spoken to funders who truly fit.
By week 12, I have a plan I can explain in one page, whatever the answer is.

title: Lead my business with integrity under pressure
who_for: Owners who feel pressure to cut corners, pay late, bribe or bend the truth to survive.
loving_god: We say plainly where we are tempted and ask God for courage to do right when it costs us.
loving_others: We tell each other the truth, share how we handled hard offers and refuse to judge a member who is struggling.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has written our own lines we will not cross, told one trusted person, and handled one real pressure without compromising.
week12_outcome: A written list of lines not to cross, shared with one person, and one pressure handled well.
arc: Write three lines you will not cross in your business, whatever it costs. Say them aloud to one person in the tribe.
Tell the tribe about one current pressure. Ask what it would look like to handle it with honesty and write your next step.
Take that step. Report what happened, what it cost and what you learned, so the tribe can pray and learn with you.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal advice or judge what a member has done. Serious wrongdoing goes to the pastor.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has faced real pressure in business and chose the harder right. Listens without shock.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I know my lines and I have told someone who will hold me to them.
By week 12, I handled a real pressure without cutting a corner.
By week 12, I lead my business with a clear conscience and I'm not alone in it.

title: Step into a leadership role
who_for: Employees who are being asked to lead, or want to be, and want to do it with integrity.
loving_god: We bring our work to God each week and ask Him to make us leaders who serve before we direct.
loving_others: We share real situations from work, listen before advising and pray for each other's teams by name, without breaking confidence.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has taken one visible leadership responsibility, asked a leader for guidance and written down how we want to lead.
week12_outcome: One visible leadership step taken, a conversation with a leader had, and a short written leadership approach.
arc: Name the leadership role you want and the three skills it needs. Rate yourself honestly on each.
Ask a leader you respect for twenty minutes and bring two questions. Act on one thing they say.
Take one visible responsibility at work, in church or in the community, and report back to the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal or HR advice and never ask members to name colleagues or share private company information.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has led people at work and can speak honestly about mistakes. Draws out others before giving an opinion.

title: Change career direction with confidence
who_for: Professionals who sense the current path is wrong and want to move wisely, not in a panic.
loving_god: We ask God what He has put in us and we are willing to wait on Him before we leap.
loving_others: We listen to each other's stories without rushing to fix them and open doors for one another where we can.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has named our strengths and interests, spoken to two people in the field and run one small test of the new direction.
week12_outcome: Strengths named, two conversations with people in the field, and one small test done.
arc: List what you enjoy, what you are good at and what the market pays for. Look for the overlap.
Speak to two people already in the field you are considering and ask what they wish they had known.
Try a small test before you commit: a short course, a side project or a week of shadowing.
guardrail: Leaders do not tell anyone to quit a job. They help members think and let them decide.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has changed careers or helped others do so, and can sit with uncertainty without hurrying people.

title: Earn a promotion or a raise I can defend
who_for: Employees who have taken on more than their title or pay reflects, and want to ask well.
loving_god: We ask God to keep us free of envy and bitterness, and to help us ask honestly and wait patiently.
loving_others: We help each other list real results, rehearse the conversation and encourage each other to ask.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written list of results with numbers, has practised the request aloud and has made it to the right person.
week12_outcome: A written list of results, a rehearsed request, and the conversation held.
arc: Write down what you delivered in the last year, with numbers where you can. Note what your manager says they value most.
Draft what you will ask for and why, in five sentences. Rehearse it aloud with someone in the tribe until you can say it calmly.
Book the conversation and hold it. Report what was said, thank the tribe, and write your next step whatever the answer was.
guardrail: Leaders do not promise a raise or give legal or HR advice. They help members prepare and leave the decision to the employer.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has asked for and received a raise or promotion with evidence, and can coach without pushing.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have made my case clearly and I'm at peace with the answer.
By week 12, I know my value in numbers and I can say it without apologising.
By week 12, I have asked for what I deserve and I did not do it alone.

title: Build a reputation for excellent work
who_for: Professionals who want to be known as dependable, skilled and fair at work.
loving_god: We treat our work as something we do for God, and we hold ourselves to the standard He would.
loving_others: We give each other honest feedback, celebrate good work and refuse to spread rumours or take credit.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has asked three colleagues for feedback, chosen one habit that improves our work and kept it every week.
week12_outcome: Feedback from three colleagues, and one improving work habit kept every week.
arc: Describe in three lines how you want colleagues to describe your work. Ask three colleagues for one honest strength and one improvement.
Pick one habit that would lift your work, such as finishing early, checking twice or replying within a day. Do it every day this month.
Ask one person who relies on you what would make you more useful. Act on the answer and tell the tribe the result.
guardrail: Leaders do not ask members to name or criticise colleagues. The tribe talks about its own habits only.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Is known for dependable work and can say how they built that. Gives plain, kind feedback.

member_outcomes: By week 12, people at work can count on me and I can say why.
By week 12, I have one habit that improved my work and I kept it.
By week 12, I have honest feedback and I used it.

title: Find a mentor, and become one
who_for: Professionals who want a guide for their next stage and someone younger to pour into.
loving_god: We thank God for the people who shaped us and ask Him to make us people who shape others well.
loving_others: We introduce each other to wise people, practise good questions and take turns being the one who listens.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has asked one person to mentor us, met them at least twice and begun to encourage someone younger.
week12_outcome: A mentor asked and met twice, and one younger person encouraged on a regular basis.
arc: Write down what you want to learn and who is already doing it. Choose one person to ask and write your request in three sentences.
Ask. Meet your mentor, bring two questions and write one thing to try. Also find one younger person you can encourage.
Meet your mentor again and report what you tried. Meet your younger person and pass on one lesson from your own life.
guardrail: Leaders do not pair members with mentors or promise that anyone will agree. Members ask for themselves.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has been mentored and mentors someone now. Warm, patient and good at asking questions.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a mentor and I'm learning from them.
By week 12, I'm encouraging someone younger and it is good for me too.
By week 12, I know how to ask for guidance and how to give it.

title: Gain a skill or certification in my field
who_for: Professionals who know one skill or certificate would open their next step.
loving_god: We study as an act of worship and ask God to give us diligence and humility.
loving_others: We hold each other to study hours, quiz one another and share notes and good resources.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has chosen the skill or certificate, kept a weekly study block and finished a defined part of it.
week12_outcome: The skill or certificate chosen, a weekly study block kept, and a defined part finished.
arc: Name the skill or certificate your next step needs, what it costs and when you want to finish. Choose one way to begin this week.
Set a weekly study block and protect it. Study with one person from the tribe once a week and quiz each other.
Finish a clear part of the course or practise paper under timed conditions. Share what you learned and what you will repeat.
guardrail: Leaders do not recommend paid courses or take payment from members. They share only free tips and what worked for them.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has earned a professional certificate while working and can share how they found the time.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I'm well on my way to the skill or certificate I chose.
By week 12, I study every week and I no longer wait for a perfect time.
By week 12, I have finished a real part of it and others are cheering me on.

title: Manage my time and energy at work
who_for: Professionals who are always busy, always behind and tired.
loving_god: We make room for rest, prayer and Sabbath because we trust God with what we cannot finish.
loving_others: We check on each other's load, share what works and say no together instead of alone.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a weekly plan we follow, one protected rest block and one habit that cuts wasted time.
week12_outcome: A weekly plan followed, a protected rest block and one time-saving habit kept.
arc: Track where your time and energy go for one week. Circle the biggest drain and the best use of your hours.
Plan each week on Sunday, with three priorities and one protected rest block. Share your plan with a partner in the tribe.
Stop or reduce one time-waster. Review the season with your partner and write the two habits you will keep.
guardrail: Leaders do not give medical or mental health advice. If a member seems unwell, they encourage them to see a professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has learned to work well without overworking. Calm and organised, not preachy about it.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I plan my week and I end more days with energy left.
By week 12, I protect one block of rest and I'm not guilty about it.
By week 12, I know what drains me and I have done something about it.

title: Handle workplace conflict with grace
who_for: Professionals in tension with a colleague, a manager or a team, who want to respond well.
loving_god: We ask God to guard our words, soften our hearts and show us our part in every conflict.
loving_others: We listen without taking sides, rehearse hard conversations and pray for the people we find difficult.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has had one honest conversation we were avoiding, owned our part and kept our tone calm.
week12_outcome: One avoided conversation held, with our own part owned and the tone calm.
arc: Describe the conflict in four sentences without blaming. Write what you want, what the other person might want and your own part.
Rehearse the conversation aloud with someone in the tribe. Hold it, starting with what you appreciate, then what you need.
Follow up with a kind message or a small act of respect. Share what changed and what you learned with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal or HR advice, and the tribe never discusses a colleague's private life. Cases of abuse or harassment go to the care ladder.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has handled a difficult workplace conflict well and can stay calm when others are upset. Does not take sides.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have had the conversation I was avoiding and the air is clearer.
By week 12, I stay calm in tension and I own my part.
By week 12, I handled the conflict with grace, whatever the other person did.

title: Plan the next five years of my career
who_for: Professionals who drift from year to year and want a prayerful, practical plan.
loving_god: We ask God to show us the work He has for us and we hold our plans loosely.
loving_others: We ask each other honest questions, share what we see in one another and keep each other accountable to the plan.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a one-page five-year plan, a plan for this year and one step taken from it.
week12_outcome: A one-page five-year plan, a plan for this year and one step taken.
arc: Write where you are now, what you enjoy and what you want more of. Ask two friends what strengths they see in you.
Draft a one-page plan for five years and a smaller plan for this year. Mark the skills, people and money you will need.
Take the first step on this year's plan. Share the plan with the tribe and agree who will ask about it in three months.
guardrail: Leaders do not predict anyone's future or tell members which job to take. They help them think and decide.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has planned a career with intention and revised the plan when life changed. Asks good questions.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a written plan for my career and I know my next step.
By week 12, I'm no longer drifting and I have people who will ask me about it.
By week 12, I have taken the first step and I'm at peace about the rest.

title: Build a steady client pipeline
who_for: Independent consultants and freelancers whose work arrives in waves and who want it to be steady.
loving_god: We ask God for provision and the discipline to ask for work without fear or pride.
loving_others: We introduce one another to clients, practise how we describe our work and celebrate every enquiry.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a list of people to contact, a weekly outreach hour kept and at least two new conversations with possible clients.
week12_outcome: A contact list, a weekly outreach hour kept, and two new client conversations.
arc: List twenty people who could hire you or refer you, and contact five this week.
Ask two past clients for a short testimonial and one introduction.
Set a weekly hour for outreach and keep it, whatever the week looks like.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or financial advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has built a consulting or freelance practice from nothing and still does outreach every week.

title: Price and package my expertise
who_for: Consultants who charge by the hour or by guesswork and want clear, confident offers.
loving_god: We ask God to free us from the fear of asking, and from the love of money, so that we price fairly.
loving_others: We review each other's offers, practise saying the price aloud and refuse to let each other undercharge.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has one clear package with a scope, a timeline and a price, and has offered it to a real client.
week12_outcome: One clear package with scope, timeline and price, offered to a real client.
arc: Write down what you charge today and what the result is worth to the client. Notice the gap.
Turn what you do into a clear package with a scope, a timeline and a price.
Raise your price for the next new client, and practise saying it aloud first.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or financial advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Sells packaged services at a fair price and can explain how they arrived at it.

title: Land my first three clients
who_for: New consultants and freelancers with skill but no regular clients.
loving_god: We bring our work to God daily and ask Him for the right first clients, not just any clients.
loving_others: We share leads, review each other's messages and give honest feedback on how we describe our work.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a clear one-sentence offer, has contacted at least thirty people and has three paying clients or the next best step.
week12_outcome: Three paying clients, or a clear next step with dates.
arc: Write one sentence that says who you help and with what. List thirty people who know someone who needs that.
Message ten people a week with a short, clear ask. Offer one free, small piece of help to build trust.
Turn your best conversation into a written offer with a price. Follow up on every open lead and report to the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or financial advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Remembers the first three clients and how uncertain it felt. Practical and encouraging.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have paying clients, or I'm close and I know my next step.
By week 12, I can say what I do in one sentence and people understand.
By week 12, I ask for work every week and I'm no longer ashamed to.

title: Turn one-off projects into retainers
who_for: Consultants who finish a project and start from nothing again.
loving_god: We ask God for a long view and for the patience to serve clients well beyond the first sale.
loving_others: We share how we propose ongoing work, role-play the conversation and cheer every renewal.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has designed an ongoing service, offered it to three past or present clients and agreed one monthly arrangement.
week12_outcome: An ongoing service designed and offered to three clients, and one monthly arrangement agreed.
arc: List your past clients and what they needed after the project ended. Write one ongoing service that meets that need.
Price the service per month with a clear scope. Practise the conversation with someone in the tribe.
Offer it to three clients and report back. Agree one arrangement and write down what you will deliver each month.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or financial advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Holds retainer clients and knows what keeps them. Good at structure and follow-through.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have an ongoing client who pays me each month.
By week 12, I no longer start from zero after each project.
By week 12, I have a clear ongoing service and I know how to offer it.

title: Build a visible expert brand
who_for: Consultants who do good work that few people know about.
loving_god: We ask God to keep our hearts humble as we make our work known and to help us speak truthfully.
loving_others: We read each other's posts and bios, share honest feedback and promote each other's work.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a clear profile, has published at least six useful pieces and has had one conversation that came from them.
week12_outcome: A clear profile, six useful pieces published, and one conversation that came from them.
arc: Write what you want to be known for, in one sentence. Update your profile so a stranger can see it in ten seconds.
Publish one useful piece a week for six weeks, such as a short post, a checklist or a case lesson. Ask the tribe for feedback first.
Reach out to three people who read your pieces. Note which pieces worked best and plan the next six.
guardrail: Leaders do not guarantee results from posting and do not ask members to share the tribe's private conversations online.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has built a name in their field through useful work and writing, and shares without boasting.

member_outcomes: By week 12, people know what I do and I have a body of useful work online.
By week 12, my profile says clearly what I offer and who it is for.
By week 12, someone has contacted me because of what I published.

title: Write proposals and contracts that protect me
who_for: Consultants who have been paid late, been asked for extra work or never had a written agreement.
loving_god: We ask God to help us keep our word and to ask others to keep theirs, without bitterness.
loving_others: We share templates, read each other's proposals and help each other say no to unfair terms.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a standard proposal, a written agreement with scope and payment terms, and has used it with a real client.
week12_outcome: A standard proposal and a written agreement with scope and payment terms, used with a client.
arc: Collect any agreement you have used. List what went wrong with clients before: late pay, extra work or unclear scope.
Draft a standard proposal and agreement covering scope, price, payment dates and changes. Have a lawyer or experienced person check it.
Use it with your next client. Share what they asked about and what you would change.
guardrail: Leaders do not write or approve contracts and do not give legal advice. They share simple templates and point to a lawyer.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has lost money to a vague agreement and now works with clear terms. Calm about hard conversations.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a written agreement and I use it every time.
By week 12, I'm paid on time because the terms were clear.
By week 12, I can say no to unfair terms without guilt.

title: Build a partner network or small team
who_for: Consultants who turn work away because they are a team of one.
loving_god: We ask God to help us share work and credit generously, and to choose partners with character.
loving_others: We introduce each other to trusted people, share referrals fairly and call each other to account if we fail a partner.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has met five possible partners, agreed terms with one and delivered or planned one shared piece of work.
week12_outcome: Five possible partners met, terms agreed with one, and a shared piece of work delivered or planned.
arc: List the kinds of work you turn away and the skills a partner would need. Write the names of ten people you trust or admire.
Meet five of them. Ask what they need, share what you need and agree how credit and money would be shared.
Agree terms with one partner in writing and plan one shared piece of work. Report how it went.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or financial advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Works with partners or a small team and knows what fair sharing looks like.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a trusted partner and we have worked or planned together.
By week 12, I no longer turn away good work because I'm alone.
By week 12, I have a network of people I trust and who trust me.

title: Set boundaries so clients do not run my week
who_for: Consultants who answer at all hours and say yes to everything.
loving_god: We keep a rest day because we trust God to provide when we stop.
loving_others: We remind each other of the lines we set, role-play saying no and celebrate each time we keep one.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has written working hours, a rule for urgent requests and one rest day we protect.
week12_outcome: Written working hours, a rule for urgent requests and one protected rest day.
arc: Write what a good week looks like and where clients break it. Choose your working hours and one rest day.
Tell your clients about your hours and how to reach you in an emergency. Practise saying the message aloud first.
Keep the hours for a month and note what clients said. Share what you will keep and adjust.
guardrail: Leaders do not give mental health advice. If a member seems overwhelmed, they encourage them to speak to a professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has set firm, kind boundaries with clients and kept their clients. Honest about how hard that was.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have working hours and my clients respect them.
By week 12, I protect a rest day and my work did not suffer.
By week 12, I say no kindly and I feel lighter.

title: Land my next role
who_for: People between jobs who want a clear search, company on the road and a role that fits.
loving_god: We trust God for provision, and we ask Him to keep us from panic and from shame.
loving_others: We share leads, review each other's applications and pray for each other before every interview.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has an up-to-date CV and profile, a weekly search rhythm and at least five conversations or interviews.
week12_outcome: An updated CV and profile, a weekly search rhythm and five conversations or interviews.
arc: Update your CV and your LinkedIn profile this week, and ask one person to read them with you.
Send five focused applications or messages a week, and ask for one introduction each week.
Keep a short list of interviews and follow-ups, and thank everyone who helped you, even if it did not lead anywhere.
guardrail: Leaders do not promise jobs or take payment for introductions. They share leads freely and honestly.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has been through a job search and can keep people moving without false cheer.

title: Retool with new skills
who_for: People between jobs who see that the roles they want ask for skills they lack.
loving_god: We use this season to grow, and we ask God for patience with the time it takes.
loving_others: We study together, check each other's progress and show our work to one another before we show it to employers.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has chosen one skill, built something small with it and shown it to someone who hires.
week12_outcome: One skill chosen, one small piece of work built, and shown to someone who hires.
arc: Pick one skill the roles you want keep asking for and find one free or low-cost way to start.
Build something small that shows the skill, such as a sample, a project or a short write-up.
Share what you built with someone who hires, and ask what would make it stronger.
guardrail: Leaders do not sell courses or take payment from members. They share only free resources and what worked for them.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has learned a new skill while out of work or retooled their career. Keeps others learning.

title: Build a CV and LinkedIn profile that gets replies
who_for: Job seekers who send applications and hear nothing.
loving_god: We ask God to help us describe our gifts honestly, without shrinking or boasting.
loving_others: We read each other's CVs with kindness and honesty, and we correct each other's language and formatting.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a one-page CV in a clear format, a complete profile, and has sent both to ten people or roles.
week12_outcome: A clear one-page CV, a complete profile, and both sent to ten people or roles.
arc: Write your achievements as results, such as what you improved, saved or built. Ask a trusted person to tell you your three strongest.
Redraft your CV to one page and match your profile to it. Have two people in the tribe read both and mark anything unclear.
Send the CV and profile to ten people or roles. Note which versions drew replies and improve the next.
guardrail: Leaders do not write members' CVs or invent achievements. Everything on a CV must be true.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has read many CVs or hired people, and can explain what makes one clear.

member_outcomes: By week 12, my CV and profile show my best work and people reply.
By week 12, I can describe what I have done in clear results.
By week 12, I have sent my best version to ten people and I'm learning from the replies.

title: Prepare for interviews and negotiate an offer
who_for: Job seekers who freeze in interviews or take the first offer without asking.
loving_god: We ask God for calm, honest words and a fair outcome.
loving_others: We hold mock interviews for each other, give plain feedback and pray before the big days.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has practised ten common questions aloud, gone through at least two mock interviews and rehearsed a salary conversation.
week12_outcome: Ten questions practised, two mock interviews done and a salary conversation rehearsed.
arc: Write answers to the ten questions you most dread. Say them aloud to a partner in the tribe until they sound like you.
Hold two mock interviews in the tribe. Ask for one thing you did well and one you must change.
Practise how you will ask about pay and conditions. After any real interview, write what went well and share it.
guardrail: Leaders do not promise outcomes or coach members to exaggerate. Honest answers only.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has hired people or interviewed well, and can give straight feedback with kindness.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I walk into an interview calm and prepared.
By week 12, I can talk about pay without fear.
By week 12, I have done real interviews and I learn from each one.

title: Earn while I search
who_for: People between jobs who need some income now without losing sight of their next role.
loving_god: We ask God to provide, and we do honest work with thanks, whatever its size.
loving_others: We share short-term work leads, encourage each other when pride gets in the way and celebrate every honest naira earned.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has found at least one source of honest income that fits our search and has kept a weekly record of what we earn.
week12_outcome: One source of honest income found, and a weekly record of what is earned.
arc: List the skills and contacts you have that someone would pay for this month. Choose one way to earn that fits your search.
Make five offers or applications for short-term work. Share leads you cannot use with the tribe.
Keep a simple record of what you earn each week. Decide how much time the work gets so your search continues.
guardrail: Leaders do not give financial, legal or immigration advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has earned between jobs through small work or a side business without losing focus.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have honest income while I look for my next role.
By week 12, I earn something each week and I'm no longer ashamed of it.
By week 12, my short-term work fits around my search.

title: Keep my confidence and routine through the wait
who_for: People between jobs whose days have lost shape and whose confidence has taken a knock.
loving_god: We tell God honestly how it feels and remember that He sees our worth when no employer does.
loving_others: We check on each other every few days, keep each other to a routine and never compare our timelines.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a daily rhythm we keep, a weekly rest and a short note to ourselves about what we are proud of.
week12_outcome: A daily rhythm kept, a weekly rest and a record of what we are proud of.
arc: Write the shape of a good day: when you rise, work, move, rest and pray. Share it with a partner in the tribe.
Keep the daily rhythm for a month. Message your partner each morning with one line about your plan.
Write ten things you are proud of from the last ten years. Read three aloud to the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give mental health advice. If a member seems very low or unsafe, they use the care ladder the same day.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has waited through a long search and stayed steady. Warm, patient and a good listener.

member_outcomes: By week 12, my days have a shape again and I get up with purpose.
By week 12, I remember my worth and I'm not waiting for a job to tell me.
By week 12, I have people I can call on a hard day.

title: Grow a network that opens doors
who_for: Job seekers who know that most roles come through people and do not know how to start.
loving_god: We ask God to help us build real friendships, not only contacts, and to give before we ask.
loving_others: We introduce each other to people, practise short conversations and thank those who help us.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has had at least ten conversations with people in our field, followed up each one and offered help to someone in return.
week12_outcome: Ten conversations with people in the field, each followed up, and help offered in return.
arc: List thirty people who work where you want to work, or who know people who do. Choose ten to contact first.
Ask for a twenty-minute conversation with each of them. Ask what they wish they had known and who else you should speak to.
Thank each person within a day, report back with one useful thing and offer to help them in some way.
guardrail: Leaders do not ask members to share contacts that belong to others without their consent. Introductions are made with permission.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has a wide, honest network and still builds it. Generous with introductions.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a wider network and people who would speak for me.
By week 12, I know how to ask for a conversation without feeling like a burden.
By week 12, at least one new door has opened through someone I met.

title: Manage money well on a reduced income
who_for: People between jobs who need a clear plan for the money they have.
loving_god: We trust God for our needs and ask Him to help us be honest and wise with what we have.
loving_others: We share what we have learned about saving, encourage each other without shame and help where we can.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written budget for the reduced income, knows how many months it lasts and has made one cut or one saving.
week12_outcome: A written budget, a clear count of how many months it lasts, and one cut or saving made.
arc: Write what comes in and what goes out each month. Mark which items are needs and which can wait.
Draw up a budget for the reduced income and work out how many months it lasts. Make one cut or one saving.
Review the budget weekly with a partner in the tribe. Plan what you will do if the search takes longer.
guardrail: Leaders do not give financial, legal or immigration advice. They point to a qualified professional. The tribe never asks members to disclose their debts.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has lived on less and kept dignity, and can talk about money without shame.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I know exactly where my money goes and how long it will last.
By week 12, I have made one real saving and I sleep better.
By week 12, I manage a smaller income with peace and a plan.

title: Decide between another job and working for myself
who_for: People between jobs who wonder whether to find a job or start something of their own.
loving_god: We ask God for wisdom, we are willing to hear no, and we do not rush because we are afraid.
loving_others: We ask each other hard, kind questions, share honest experience of both paths and respect each person's choice.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has weighed both paths on paper, tested one with real people and made a written decision with a start date.
week12_outcome: Both paths weighed on paper, one tested with real people, and a written decision with a start date.
arc: Write what you would gain and lose on each path: money, time, risk, fit and family. Ask the tribe what they notice.
Test one path with real people. Apply for a role or talk to ten possible customers, and write what you hear.
Make a written decision with a date to begin and a plan for the first month. Share it with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not tell anyone which path to take. They help members think and decide for themselves.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has faced this choice and made it. Even-handed about both paths and comfortable with uncertainty.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have decided and I'm at peace with the reasons.
By week 12, I have tested my choice with real people before I committed.
By week 12, I have a start date and a plan for my first month.

title: Thrive in a long-distance family
who_for: People living apart from close family who want to stay close in heart and in habit.
loving_god: We bring our families to God by name each week and trust Him to hold them where we cannot.
loving_others: We share what works for staying close, pray for each other's families and notice when someone is carrying homesickness.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a regular time to call each close family member, one shared activity each month and a message of thanks sent.
week12_outcome: Regular calls kept, one shared monthly activity and a message of thanks sent.
arc: Agree a regular time to call each close family member, and keep to it for the whole season.
Plan one thing to do together online each month, such as a meal, a prayer, a game or a devotional.
Write a letter or voice note of thanks to someone at home and send it.
guardrail: Leaders do not take sides in family disputes or give counselling. Serious needs go to the care ladder.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Lives or has lived far from family and stayed close. Warm and attentive to people who feel alone.

title: Make a cross-border move well
who_for: People planning to move to another country, or in the first months after a move.
loving_god: We bring each step of the move to God and ask Him to go before us.
loving_others: We share lists, contacts and honest lessons, and we welcome each other as neighbours before we arrive.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a dated move plan, has spoken with someone already there and has a plan for finding a church family on arrival.
week12_outcome: A dated move plan, a conversation with someone already there, and a plan to find a church family.
arc: Write the full list of what the move needs: documents, money, housing and people. Put a date next to each item.
Find one person already living where you are going and ask what they would do differently.
Plan your first month there, including how you will find a church family from week one.
guardrail: Leaders do not give immigration, legal or tax advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has moved country and can explain the real costs and surprises. Practical and encouraging.

title: Settle in a new country and find my footing
who_for: People who have recently moved abroad and are working out daily life, work and friendship.
loving_god: We thank God for where we are, ask Him to show us why He has placed us here and trust Him through the strangeness.
loving_others: We welcome the newest person first, share local knowledge and remember that every one of us was new once.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a daily routine, three local friendships started and one way we are serving where we live.
week12_outcome: A daily routine, three local friendships started and one way of serving locally.
arc: Write what is hardest about the new place and what is already good. Set a simple daily routine and share it with the tribe.
Say hello to three neighbours or colleagues and arrange one coffee or meal. Try one local place or activity each week.
Find one way to give your time where you live. Tell the tribe what you have learned about the place and the people.
guardrail: Leaders do not give immigration, legal or tax advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has settled abroad and remembers the first months. Good at welcoming and at practical tips.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I feel more at home and I know my way around.
By week 12, I have friends where I live and a place to serve.
By week 12, I have stopped waiting to feel settled and started to live here.

title: Plan a return home well
who_for: People living abroad who are thinking of going back, or have decided to.
loving_god: We ask God to show us when and how to return, and to go back with open hands and a thankful heart.
loving_others: We help each other count the cost, share honest stories of returning and pray for those at home who wait for us.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written return plan with dates, money, work and housing, and has spoken with family and our home church.
week12_outcome: A written return plan with dates, money, work and housing, and conversations held with family and home church.
arc: Write why you want to return, what you will miss and what you must settle before you go. Share it with the tribe.
List what a return needs: money, work, housing, papers and school for any children. Put a date and a person next to each item.
Speak with family and your home church about the plan. Write the first three things you will do on arrival.
guardrail: Leaders do not give immigration, legal or tax advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has returned home after living abroad, or is planning to, and can speak about both the joy and the cost.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a clear plan for going home and I know what it will cost.
By week 12, my family and church know my plan and are ready.
By week 12, I'm at peace about the decision, whether I go this year or later.

title: Find a church family where I now live
who_for: People abroad or in a new city who miss the family of their home church.
loving_god: We ask God to lead us to a place to belong and a place to serve, and we give thanks before we find it.
loving_others: We share where we have visited, pray for each other's search and encourage each other to go back more than once.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has visited at least three churches, chosen one to join and met a few people there by name.
week12_outcome: Three churches visited, one chosen to join, and a few people there known by name.
arc: List what matters to you in a church. Look up three churches near you and choose a Sunday to visit each.
Visit each one and write what you noticed. Introduce yourself to at least two people and ask about their lives.
Choose a church to join and tell them you are coming back. Offer to help with one small task.
guardrail: Leaders do not criticise other churches or push anyone toward a church. Each member decides for themselves.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has found a church family far from home and can explain how long it took. Gentle and encouraging.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I belong to a church family where I live.
By week 12, I know people by name at my church and they know me.
By week 12, I'm serving somewhere, even in a small way.

title: Support my parents from a distance
who_for: Adult children abroad who carry worry and responsibility for ageing parents back home.
loving_god: We bring our parents to God each week and ask Him for peace about what we cannot do from afar.
loving_others: We listen to each other's worries without rushing to fix them and share what has helped us care well from far away.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a regular call schedule with our parents, a shared plan with our siblings and one practical support in place.
week12_outcome: A regular call schedule, a plan agreed with siblings and one practical support in place.
arc: Write what your parents most need and what you can do from where you are. Agree call times with them and keep them.
Talk with your siblings or a trusted relative about who does what. Put one practical support in place, such as a regular visitor or a monthly check.
Review the plan with your parents and your siblings. Share one honest struggle with the tribe and ask for prayer.
guardrail: Leaders do not give medical, legal or financial advice. If a member is under strain, they use the care ladder.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has cared for parents from abroad and knows the guilt and the cost. Steady and compassionate.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I speak with my parents on a regular schedule and I'm less anxious.
By week 12, my family has a plan so I'm not carrying this alone.
By week 12, I have put practical support in place for my parents.

title: Handle papers, taxes and money across borders
who_for: People abroad who deal with visas, tax forms, bank accounts and sending money home.
loving_god: We ask God for honesty in every form and every transfer, and for peace when the process is slow.
loving_others: We share what we have learned about the process, encourage each other to ask professionals and remind each other of deadlines.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a list of every paper and deadline that applies to us, a place to keep documents and an appointment booked where we need help.
week12_outcome: A list of every paper and deadline, a safe place for documents and help booked where needed.
arc: List every paper, permit, tax form and account you need in the countries involved. Write the deadline next to each.
Collect your documents in one safe place, with copies. Book help from a qualified person for anything you are unsure of.
Set reminders for every deadline and review the list monthly with a partner in the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give immigration, legal or tax advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has handled papers and money across countries carefully. Patient and organised, and clear about what they do not know.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I know what papers and deadlines I have and none are a surprise.
By week 12, my documents are in order and help is booked where I need it.
By week 12, I handle money across borders openly and with a plan.

title: Raise children rooted in our culture and faith abroad
who_for: Parents raising children abroad who want them to keep their language, culture and faith.
loving_god: We ask God to give our children a faith of their own and to help us teach it with joy.
loving_others: We swap ideas for stories, food, language and festivals, and we share the pressures our children face.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a weekly family time for faith and culture, and one new practice our children have taken part in.
week12_outcome: A weekly family time for faith and culture, and one new shared practice.
arc: Write three things you want your children to carry from home. Choose one weekly time to share them as a family.
Add one new practice each month, such as a language night, a home dish or a Bible story told in your language.
Ask your children what they enjoyed and what they found hard. Share the answers and your next steps with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not criticise another family's choices or give parenting rules. They share ideas and let each parent decide.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has raised children abroad with faith and culture intact, or is doing so now. Warm, practical and open to other views.

member_outcomes: By week 12, our family has a weekly time that our children look forward to.
By week 12, my children know more of our language, stories and faith.
By week 12, I feel less alone in raising children away from home.

title: Strengthen our marriage
who_for: Married couples who want a stronger marriage and are willing to do small things every week.
loving_god: We pray for our spouse and with our spouse every week, and put God at the centre of our decisions.
loving_others: We listen before we respond, serve each other every day, and settle hurts quickly instead of keeping score.
loving_life: By week 12 we have a monthly date, a shared budget and one new habit we have kept for twelve weeks.
week12_outcome: A monthly date, a shared budget and one habit kept.
arc: Set a weekly time to talk, with phones away, and begin each time by naming one thing you appreciate.
Pray together every day this month, even for two minutes.
Plan one date or day away that you both look forward to, and agree what you want it to do for the marriage.
guardrail: Leaders host and encourage. They do not counsel couples or take sides. Serious cases go to the care ladder.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has a marriage that has been tested and held. Humble, warm and discreet. Never presents their own marriage as the model.

title: Prepare well for marriage
who_for: Engaged couples, and people in a serious relationship heading toward marriage.
loving_god: We ask God to prepare us as people before we prepare for a wedding, and we pray for our future home.
loving_others: We ask each other honest questions, listen to couples who have gone before us and respect each person's pace and purity.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has talked openly about money, children, family and faith, and has booked pre-marriage counselling or a class.
week12_outcome: Money, children, family and faith discussed openly, and pre-marriage counselling or a class booked.
arc: Write what you hope for in a marriage and what you are growing in. Share it with a trusted mentor.
Talk openly about money, children, family and faith, and note where you agree and where you do not.
Book your pre-marriage counselling or class, and ask a married couple to walk with you.
guardrail: Leaders do not counsel couples or advise on whether to marry. They host, encourage and point to the pastoral team.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Married for several years and willing to speak plainly about preparation. Discreet and warm.

title: Rebuild after a relationship ends
who_for: People recovering from a broken engagement, a breakup, a divorce or the loss of a spouse, who want company and a steady way forward.
loving_god: We bring our grief and our questions to God honestly and trust Him to heal at a pace that is right for each of us.
loving_others: We listen without fixing, keep each other's stories private and show up for each other on the hard days.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a daily habit that steadies us, one safe person we talk to often and a clear next step for the season ahead.
week12_outcome: A steadying daily habit, a safe person to talk to and one clear next step.
arc: Give yourself space to grieve, and tell one safe person how you are really doing.
Return to one habit that keeps you steady, such as prayer, exercise, rest or time with friends.
Name what you want to carry forward and what you are leaving behind, and share it with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not counsel or diagnose, and never press anyone to share more than they want to. Serious grief or risk goes to the care ladder the same day.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has walked through a loss themselves, or has long experience of sitting with people in grief. Gentle, patient and discreet.

title: Communicate and resolve conflict in marriage
who_for: Married couples who keep having the same argument and want better ways to speak and listen.
loving_god: We ask God to soften our hearts, show us our own part and teach us to speak with patience.
loving_others: We share what has helped us, never share what our spouse told us in confidence and refuse to take sides.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has practised a calm way of raising a problem, agreed a rule for arguing and used it at least three times.
week12_outcome: A calm way of raising problems, a rule for arguing and its use at least three times.
arc: Write the argument you repeat and how it usually ends. Each of you describes your own part, without the other's.
Agree one rule for hard conversations, such as no phones, a pause when voices rise or one person speaks at a time. Use it three times.
Say thank you for one thing your spouse did in a hard moment. Share one thing you will keep doing with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not counsel couples or take sides. If there is fear, control or violence in a marriage, they use the care ladder the same day.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has worked at communication in their own marriage and can say how. Calm in tension and impartial.

member_outcomes: By week 12, we argue less and we repair faster.
By week 12, we can raise a problem without it turning into a fight.
By week 12, we have a rule for hard moments and we use it.

title: Manage money together as a couple
who_for: Married or engaged couples who disagree about money, or never talk about it.
loving_god: We thank God for what we have, ask for wisdom and generosity and agree to give before we spend.
loving_others: We share what has worked for us, keep each couple's figures private and encourage openness without pressure.
loving_life: By week 12 each couple has talked openly about income, debts and giving, written a shared budget and held a monthly money meeting three times.
week12_outcome: Income, debts and giving discussed openly, a shared budget written and three monthly money meetings held.
arc: Each of you writes what money means to you and what you fear. Share it with each other and do not argue about it.
