Invite someone who has never played with you. Share what the games have done for your body and your friendships.
guardrail: Leaders do not give medical advice, diets or exercise for a condition. Members see a doctor first where there is any doubt. Anyone returning from injury checks with a doctor first.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Plays a team sport regularly and organises games fairly. Warm, inclusive and never a bully on the pitch.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I play every week and I look forward to it.
By week 12, I have made new friends through the game.
By week 12, I'm fitter and I laugh more.

title: Build healthy habits as a family
who_for: Families who want to eat, move and rest better together.
loving_god: We care for our bodies as a family because we belong to God, and we thank Him for each other.
loving_others: We share ideas, join each other for family walks and games and never shame a child about their body.
loving_life: By week 12 each family has a weekly active outing, three family meals a week and one agreed habit each member keeps.
week12_outcome: A weekly active family outing, three family meals a week and one agreed habit each.
arc: Ask each person in the family what healthy habit they would try. Choose one family habit everyone agrees on.
Plan a weekly active outing, such as a walk, a game or a bike ride. Cook and eat together three times a week.
Give each person one habit of their own. Share what worked and what the children said with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give medical advice, diets or exercise for a condition. Members see a doctor first where there is any doubt. The tribe never comments on a child's weight.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has built healthy habits with their own family, with humour and patience. Never a nag.

member_outcomes: By week 12, our family moves and eats better together.
By week 12, we share meals and the children help cook.
By week 12, healthy habits feel like fun and not punishment.

title: Excel in my studies or exams
who_for: Students at any level who want to study well, stay steady under pressure and finish strong.
loving_god: We study as an act of worship, we rest on the day set apart and we trust God with the results.
loving_others: We study together, explain hard ideas to each other and encourage anyone who is afraid.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a study timetable we keep, a weekly study partner and at least two timed practice papers done.
week12_outcome: A study timetable kept, a weekly study partner and two timed practice papers done.
arc: Make a study timetable that fits your real life, and share it with one person who will ask how it is going.
Study with one or two others once a week and teach each other the hardest topics.
Do past papers under timed conditions, and learn from every mistake.
guardrail: Leaders do not do members' work for them or help anyone cheat. They help members study honestly.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has studied hard and honestly, and can explain how they kept going. Patient with those who are afraid of exams.

title: Grow as an educator
who_for: Teachers, lecturers and trainers who want to grow in their craft and in their care for learners.
loving_god: We see our teaching as a calling, and we ask God for patience, wisdom and a heart for every learner.
loving_others: We watch each other's lessons kindly, share what worked and pray for our classes and students by first name only.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has chosen one thing to improve, tried a new method and had a colleague watch a lesson.
week12_outcome: One teaching skill chosen, a new method tried and a lesson watched by a colleague.
arc: Choose one thing in your teaching to improve this season and ask a colleague to watch one lesson.
Try one new method with your class and note what the students say.
Write down one lesson you will keep and share it with another teacher.
guardrail: Leaders never share names, records or private details of any student. Only first names, and only with care.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Teaches well and keeps learning. Generous with their classroom and open to feedback.

title: Pass a professional or entrance exam
who_for: Anyone preparing for a professional, licensing or entrance exam, and who needs a plan and company.
loving_god: We prepare with diligence and then trust God with the result, and we ask Him to keep our minds calm.
loving_others: We set a study rhythm together, quiz one another and pray for each other on the days that matter.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has covered the syllabus on a plan, done at least three timed papers and booked the exam or the date.
week12_outcome: The syllabus covered on a plan, three timed papers done and the exam date booked.
arc: Get the full syllabus and the exam date. Divide the syllabus into twelve weeks and mark the weak topics.
Study to the plan each week and meet a partner to quiz each other on the hardest topics. Do one timed paper a fortnight.
Do timed papers under exam conditions and learn from each mistake. Plan the final week with rest and prayer.
guardrail: Leaders do not share or look for leaked questions and never help anyone cheat. They study honestly.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has passed a professional or entrance exam and can explain how they prepared. Calm and organised.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I'm ready for the exam and I have covered the syllabus.
By week 12, I have practised under exam conditions and I'm calmer.
By week 12, I have people who prayed with me and I'm not alone.

title: Finish my dissertation or project on time
who_for: Students and researchers with a dissertation, thesis or long project that is stuck or slipping.
loving_god: We bring our work to God, ask Him for clear thinking and for strength to finish what we began.
loving_others: We set deadlines for each other, read each other's drafts and celebrate every chapter.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a chapter plan with dates, writes at fixed times each week and has handed a draft to a reader.
week12_outcome: A chapter plan with dates, fixed writing times and a draft handed to a reader.
arc: Write what is left to do and when it is due, chapter by chapter. Choose fixed writing times each week and tell the tribe.
Write at your fixed times and report your word count or pages each week. Send a draft chapter to a reader and ask for honest comments.
Edit one chapter at a time and finish the draft. Plan the final week before the deadline with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not write, edit or rewrite members' work and never help anyone plagiarise. They help members plan and keep going.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has finished a long piece of academic work, and remembers the middle slump. Encouraging and firm about deadlines.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a full draft or my project is on track to finish on time.
By week 12, I write at fixed times and I no longer wait to feel ready.
By week 12, I have a reader and people cheering me on.

title: Build study habits that last
who_for: Students who study in bursts, cram at the last minute and want a routine they can keep.
loving_god: We treat our minds as a gift and ask God to give us focus and a love for learning.
loving_others: We study together, keep each other accountable and share the methods that work.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a daily study time, a place and method that work for us and a weekly review we keep.
week12_outcome: A daily study time, a place and method that work, and a weekly review kept.
arc: Track when and where you study well for one week. Choose a daily study time and a place that has few distractions.
Try one new method, such as testing yourself or teaching a friend, for a month. Share what you notice with a study partner.
Do a short weekly review of what you learned and what you will do next. Keep the habits you want for next term.
guardrail: Leaders do not do members' work or give medical advice. If a student seems unwell or overwhelmed, they encourage them to speak to a professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Studies steadily and can explain their own habits. Warm and free of pressure.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I study at the same time most days without a fight.
By week 12, I understand more and cram less.
By week 12, I have a method that works and a partner to keep me going.

title: Win a scholarship or a place abroad
who_for: Students and graduates applying for a scholarship, a fellowship or a place at a school or university abroad.
loving_god: We ask God to open the right door, and we apply with honesty, humility and thankfulness.
loving_others: We read each other's essays, practise interviews and share leads without hoarding them.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a shortlist of programmes, a draft personal statement read by two people and at least two complete applications sent.
week12_outcome: A shortlist of programmes, a personal statement read by two people and two applications sent.
arc: List five programmes that fit you and what each one asks for. Put every deadline in your calendar.
Write your personal statement, true to your story, and give it to two readers. Gather the documents and referees each programme needs.
Send at least two complete applications before their deadlines. Plan how you will respond to a yes or a no.
guardrail: Leaders do not pay for or arrange admission or visas, and do not give immigration advice. They share only honest help.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has won a scholarship or studied abroad, or helped others do so. Honest about rejections.

member_outcomes: By week 12, my applications are sent and I did my best.
By week 12, I can tell my story clearly in writing.
By week 12, I have people who prayed and worked with me.

title: Lead a classroom with calm and confidence
who_for: Teachers, especially new ones, who struggle with discipline, noise and nerves.
loving_god: We ask God to give us calm authority and a heart for the children in front of us.
loving_others: We swap classroom ideas, role-play hard moments and encourage each other on the worst days.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a clear routine for the start and end of lessons, a simple set of class rules and one lesson watched and discussed with a colleague.
week12_outcome: Routines for the start and end of lessons, simple class rules and one lesson discussed with a colleague.
arc: Write the three moments in class that drain you most. Choose one routine for starting lessons and one for ending them.
Agree a few clear class rules and explain them calmly. Practise your opening lines aloud with someone in the tribe.
Ask a colleague to watch a lesson and give two comments. Share what you will keep, and what you will change.
guardrail: Leaders never discuss pupils by name or share school records. Concerns about a child's safety go to the school and the care ladder.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Teaches with calm authority and remembers their early struggles. Encouraging and practical.

member_outcomes: By week 12, my lessons start and end with calm and routine.
By week 12, I handle disruption without shouting.
By week 12, I enjoy my class more and I'm not alone in the hard days.

title: Start or grow a school, tutoring or training venture
who_for: Educators and entrepreneurs starting or growing a school, a tutoring service or a training programme.
loving_god: We ask God to make our work a blessing to children and families, and to keep our motives clean.
loving_others: We share what we learn about running a venture, visit each other's work and refer learners honestly.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written plan for who we serve, what it costs and the income it needs, and has enrolled or contacted our first learners.
week12_outcome: A written plan for learners, costs and income, and first learners enrolled or contacted.
arc: Write who you will serve, what they need and what you will charge. Visit one working school or tutoring service and ask what they wish they had known.
Find out the registration and safety rules that apply. Write a simple budget for the first term.
Enrol or contact your first learners. Share what happened and what you will change next term.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, tax or regulatory advice and do not endorse any venture to the church. Members must follow the rules for schools and child safety.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has run or helped run a school or training venture and knows the rules and the real costs. Careful about children's safety.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a clear plan and my first learners.
By week 12, I know the rules, the costs and the risks of my venture.
By week 12, I'm no longer building this alone.

title: Choose a course or career path with clarity
who_for: Students and school leavers who must choose a course, a school or a first career and feel pressure from many sides.
loving_god: We ask God what He has placed in us, and we are willing to hear Him through counsel and through our own gifts.
loving_others: We listen without pushing our own plans, share honest stories of the paths we took and respect each person's choice.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has listed our strengths and interests, spoken with three people in fields we are considering and written our decision with reasons.
week12_outcome: Strengths and interests listed, three conversations held, and a written decision with reasons.
arc: List what you enjoy, what you are good at and what matters to you. Ask three people who know you well what strengths they see.
Speak with three people in fields you are considering and ask what a normal week looks like. Find out what each course really requires.
Write your decision and your reasons, and share them with your family and the tribe. Plan your next step and date.
guardrail: Leaders do not tell anyone what to study or pressure them toward a field. They ask questions and the member decides, with their family.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Chose a path with care and can talk about their detours without pressure. Patient with young people and their families.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have chosen my path and I know why.
By week 12, I understand what my choice will ask of me.
By week 12, I'm at peace with my decision and my family knows it.

title: Sustain my calling without burning out
who_for: Doctors, nurses, pharmacists and health workers who feel the weight of the work and want to keep going well.
loving_god: We keep a daily pause with God, even five minutes between shifts, and treat our work as a calling, not only a job.
loving_others: We check on each other between shifts, carry each other's prayer needs, and say no to over-giving together.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a rest day we protect, a sleep pattern that works and one work boundary we have kept.
week12_outcome: A protected rest day and one kept work boundary.
arc: List what drains you and what restores you. Protect one restoring thing this week.
Set one boundary on your time and tell someone who will help you keep it.
Plan a proper rest, a day or more, in the next quarter and put it in your calendar now.
guardrail: Leaders give no medical advice and never discuss patients. Names and cases stay out of the tribe.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has worked in healthcare long enough to know the cost, and has learned to rest. Gentle, discreet and not heroic.

title: Advance my specialisation
who_for: Health workers working toward a specialty, a higher qualification or a senior post.
loving_god: We see our training as stewardship of a gift, and we ask God for diligence and humility.
loving_others: We share study plans, prepare each other for exams and interviews and celebrate every step.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has the next exam, certificate or posting written with a date, a mentor in view and a weekly study block we keep.
week12_outcome: The next qualification written with a date, a mentor in view and a weekly study block kept.
arc: Write the next exam, certificate or posting you need and the date you want it by.
Find a mentor already where you want to be and ask for a regular conversation.
Set a weekly study block and protect it, even on busy weeks.
guardrail: Leaders give no medical advice and never discuss patients. Names and cases stay out of the tribe.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has progressed through specialist training and knows the demands. Practical and supportive.

title: Prepare for my licensing or exit exams
who_for: Doctors, nurses, pharmacists and other health workers preparing for a licensing or exit exam.
loving_god: We prepare with diligence, rest on the day set apart and trust God with the result.
loving_others: We quiz each other, share notes and pray for each other before the exams.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has covered the syllabus on a plan, done timed practice papers and booked a date for the exam.
week12_outcome: The syllabus covered on a plan, timed practice papers done and the exam date booked.
arc: Get the syllabus and the exam date. Divide the topics into twelve weeks and mark the ones you find hardest.
Protect a study block each week, even on heavy shifts. Quiz a partner in the tribe on the hardest topics.
Do timed practice papers and learn from every error. Plan the final week with rest and prayer.
guardrail: Leaders give no medical advice and never discuss patients. Names and cases stay out of the tribe. They never share or look for leaked questions.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has passed licensing or exit exams while working and can explain how they found time to study. Calm and organised.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I'm ready for the exam and I have a plan for the last weeks.
By week 12, I study every week even when my shifts are heavy.
By week 12, I have people who study with me and pray for me.

title: Care with compassion at the bedside
who_for: Nurses, doctors and carers who want to stay kind and present while the work is relentless.
loving_god: We ask God to see each patient through His eyes, and to keep our hearts soft when we are tired.
loving_others: We share the hardest moments without naming patients, pray for each other and remind each other of why we began.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a short habit that brings us back to the person in the bed, a way of resetting after hard cases and one kind act each shift.
week12_outcome: A habit that brings us back to the person, a way of resetting after hard cases and one kind act each shift.
arc: Write what first drew you to this work and what has worn it down. Choose a short habit to pause before each patient, such as one breath and one prayer.
Each shift, do one small act of kindness that costs you nothing. Share one story with the tribe, with no names or details.
Find a way to reset after a hard case, such as a walk, a call or a prayer. Tell the tribe what has helped.
guardrail: Leaders give no medical advice and never discuss patients. Names and cases stay out of the tribe. Anything that harms a patient or a colleague goes to the right authority and the care ladder.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has cared at the bedside for years and kept a soft heart. Honest about compassion fatigue and discreet.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I'm more present with my patients, even on tired days.
By week 12, I have a way to reset after hard cases.
By week 12, I remember why I do this work and I'm not carrying it alone.

title: Serve underserved communities through outreach
who_for: Health workers who want to give their skills to communities that cannot easily afford care.
loving_god: We see outreach as love of neighbour, and we ask God to keep our hearts humble and our work honest.
loving_others: We plan together, share transport and supplies and learn from each other's experience of the field.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has joined or planned a community outreach with a clear purpose, a team and a date, and has served at least once.
week12_outcome: A community outreach planned or joined, with a clear purpose, a team and a date, and at least one service given.
arc: Choose a community and a need. Find out who already serves there and how you can join or partner with them.
Plan the outreach with a team: purpose, date, supplies, transport and safety. Get permission from the right people.
Serve at least once and write what you learned. Share with the tribe what you will do next.
guardrail: Leaders do not treat patients through the tribe, give medical advice or promise treatment. All outreach follows the rules for health workers and child safety.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has served on outreach and understands the preparation it needs. Humble, organised and safety-minded.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have served a community with my skills.
By week 12, I have a team and a plan for serving again.
By week 12, my work feels bigger than a job.

title: Build a private practice or health business
who_for: Health professionals who want to start or grow a clinic, a pharmacy, a laboratory or another health business.
loving_god: We ask God to make our work a blessing to patients and to keep us honest in every bill and every record.
loving_others: We share what we learn about licences, staff and equipment, and we refer to one another honestly.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written plan covering licence, location, costs and first patients, and has spoken to at least three people who run similar businesses.
week12_outcome: A written plan covering licence, location, costs and first patients, and three conversations with people who run similar businesses.
arc: Write what service you want to offer, who for and where. Find out what licences and approvals you need.
Speak to three people who run similar services and ask about costs, staff and surprises. Build a simple budget for the first six months.
Take the next legal or practical step, such as a licence application or a location visit. Share your plan with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal, regulatory, tax or medical advice. All practice must follow the rules for health professionals in Nigeria.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has built or run a health business and understands both care and cost. Honest about what went wrong.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a clear plan for my practice or business.
By week 12, I know the licences, costs and risks involved.
By week 12, I have people who have done this walking with me.

title: Lead a ward or team well
who_for: Nurses, doctors and managers who lead a ward, unit or team and want to do it with fairness and care.
loving_god: We lead as servants, ask God for wisdom in hard decisions and pray for the people we supervise.
loving_others: We share real leadership problems without naming staff or patients, and learn from each other's mistakes.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a weekly check-in with our team, a fair way of sharing hard shifts and one difficult conversation held with care.
week12_outcome: A weekly team check-in, a fair way of sharing hard shifts and one difficult conversation held with care.
arc: Write what your team needs from you most and where you fall short. Ask two team members for honest comments.
Start a short weekly check-in with your team and create a fair rota for hard shifts. Share what you learn with the tribe.
Hold the one difficult conversation you have been putting off, with care. Report how it went and what you will do next.
guardrail: Leaders give no medical advice and never discuss patients. Names and cases stay out of the tribe. They never discuss individual staff by name.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Leads a clinical team and values fairness and kindness over control. Calm under pressure.

member_outcomes: By week 12, my team knows what to expect from me and I know what they need.
By week 12, I share hard work more fairly.
By week 12, I lead with more calm and less fear.

title: Plan a move to practise abroad, or a return home
who_for: Health workers thinking of practising in another country, or returning home after practising abroad.
loving_god: We ask God where He wants us to serve, and we move only with open hands and a thankful heart.
loving_others: We share honest stories of leaving and returning, count the cost together and pray for those we leave behind.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a written plan covering exams, registration, money and family, and has spoken to two people who have made the same move.
week12_outcome: A written plan covering exams, registration, money and family, and two conversations with people who made the same move.
arc: Write why you are considering the move and what you would gain and lose. Share it with your family and the tribe.
List what the move requires: exams, registration, money, papers and family plans. Put a date next to each item.
Speak to two people who made the same move and ask what they would do differently. Write your decision and next step.
guardrail: Leaders do not give immigration, licensing or financial advice. They share only their own experience and point to official sources.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has practised abroad or returned home and can speak about the real costs of both. Honest and balanced.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a clear plan and I know what the move will cost.
By week 12, my family and I have talked openly about the decision.
By week 12, I'm at peace about the next step, whichever way it goes.

title: Mentor younger colleagues and students
who_for: Experienced health workers who want to guide younger colleagues and students with care.
loving_god: We thank God for those who taught us and ask Him to make us patient, honest teachers.
loving_others: We share what works in teaching, encourage each other when mentoring is hard and never speak badly of a student.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has met one younger colleague or student every two weeks, taught one practical skill and listened to one of their struggles.
week12_outcome: Meetings with a younger colleague or student every two weeks, one practical skill taught and one struggle heard.
arc: Choose a younger colleague or student to mentor and agree how often you will meet. Ask what they most need to learn.
Teach one practical skill and show them how you handle a hard moment. Listen to one struggle without fixing it.
Ask them what has helped and what has not. Share what you have learned about mentoring with the tribe.
guardrail: Leaders give no medical advice and never discuss patients. Names and cases stay out of the tribe. They never discuss students or colleagues by name outside the pair.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has taught and mentored in clinical settings and does so with kindness. Patient and a good listener.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I'm mentoring someone and they are learning from me.
By week 12, I have learned how to teach with patience.
By week 12, I have given back some of what I was given.

title: Finish and release a body of work
who_for: Makers who have started more than they have finished and want to finish and share one piece of work.
loving_god: We offer our work to God as an act of worship and ask Him for the courage to finish and to share.
loving_others: We give honest, kind feedback, keep each other to deadlines and show up when work is released.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has defined what finished means, worked on it most days and shared it with a small audience.
week12_outcome: A defined piece of work finished and shared with a small audience.
arc: Choose the work you will finish. Write what finished means, and the date.
Work on it at the same time every day for a month, and mark each day you do.
Release it to a small audience first, and ask three people for honest feedback.
guardrail: Leaders do not judge anyone's faith by the style or subject of their work. Content must be fit for a church family.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has finished and released creative work and knows the struggle between starting and finishing. Honest and encouraging.

title: Turn my craft into income
who_for: Makers who want their craft to earn, without losing their joy or their integrity.
loving_god: We bring our gifts to God, and we ask for wisdom to price, sell and give with a clean heart.
loving_others: We share leads, introduce each other to buyers and tell each other honestly what we think of each other's prices.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has clear prices, a place to sell and offered our work to at least ten people.
week12_outcome: Clear prices, a place to sell and the work offered to ten people.
arc: Decide who would pay for your craft and what they would pay for, and ask three of them.
Put a price on one thing you make and offer it to ten people this month.
Set up a simple way to be paid and to be found, such as a page, a profile or an account.
guardrail: Leaders do not give legal or financial advice. They point to a qualified professional.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Earns from creative work and speaks honestly about the money side. Practical and generous.

title: Build a consistent creative practice
who_for: Makers who create in bursts and want a steady rhythm, however small.
loving_god: We make as an act of thanks to the Creator, and we ask Him to make our hands steady and our hearts free.
loving_others: We keep each other to the hours we set, share work in progress and never mock rough drafts.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has made something on most days we planned, has a fixed creative time and has shown unfinished work to the tribe.
week12_outcome: A fixed creative time kept, work made on most planned days and unfinished work shown.
arc: Choose a daily or weekly creative time you can keep on a bad day. Set a small target, such as ten minutes or one page.
Keep the time for a month and mark each day on a calendar. Show a piece of work in progress to the tribe each week.
Review what helped and what blocked you. Set the practice for the next season.
guardrail: Leaders do not judge anyone's faith by the style or subject of their work. Content must be fit for a church family.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Keeps a regular creative practice and treats it as work. Gentle with those who struggle to start.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I make something regularly and I no longer wait for inspiration.
By week 12, I have shown my unfinished work and survived it.
By week 12, my practice has a place in my week.

title: Grow an audience that cares
who_for: Makers who share their work online or in person and want a small, real audience.
loving_god: We share our work to bless people, and we ask God to guard us from chasing numbers.
loving_others: We encourage each other's work in public, give honest feedback in private and refuse to buy followers.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has shared our work on a regular schedule, replied to everyone who responded and built a list of at least fifty people who want to hear from us.
week12_outcome: Work shared on a regular schedule, every reply answered and a list of fifty interested people.
arc: Write who your work is for and what you want them to feel. Choose one place where those people already are.
Share your work on a regular schedule and reply to every person who responds. Ask three people what they would like more of.
Start a simple list of people who want to hear from you. Keep what worked and drop what did not.
guardrail: Leaders do not promise followers or income, and do not endorse buying likes or followers. They share only honest ideas.

hidden_only_pastorate.who_leads_well: Has built a real audience slowly and cares for the people in it more than the numbers.

member_outcomes: By week 12, I have a small audience that truly cares about my work.
By week 12, I share on a schedule I can keep.
By week 12, I know who my work is for and I talk to them.

title: Win my first paid commissions
who_for: Makers whose work people admire but have not yet paid for.
loving_god: We ask God for the right first clients and for humility in the work and in the asking.
loving_others: We share leads, review each other's offers and encourage each other to ask for payment.
loving_life: By week 12 each of us has a portfolio of three pieces, a clear price for a commission and at least one paid commission agreed or finished.
week12_outcome: A portfolio of three pieces, a clear commission price and one paid commission agreed or finished.
